channel.title: The Rift Archive — chronology
channel.description: Dated entries from the world of Konflikt ’47, from the Green Vault's years in shadow to the Rift War of 1947.

item.title: The war moves west
item.description: The second Rift War volume turns to the Pacific and the Japanese threat to the American mainland.

item.title: Dresden Defiant
item.description: The final chapter of the first volume: the Rift city, and everyone who wants it.

item.title: Operation Valentine, second phase
item.description: The offensive resumes with the Axis line bent but not broken.

item.title: Operation Touchdown
item.description: The Allies go into Germany itself, with Roberta Wells and the 109th Airborne leading.

item.title: Festung Europa begins
item.description: The Rift War series opens in Normandy: the Allies still cannot break the Axis, and Dresden is the prize.

item.title: Operation Valentine, first phase
item.description: A second offensive opens in February and grinds for five months.

item.title: Operation Pluto
item.description: The first Allied push of the Rift War year opens in the west.

item.title: The Conference on Necromobilization
item.description: The Allies convene to decide what, legally and morally, the dead are.

item.title: The Automated Battalion
item.description: Commonwealth industry begins replacing infantry sections with machines that do not flinch.

item.title: The stalemate hardens
item.description: Three blocs, four Rifts, no decisive advantage. Europe becomes an arms race with a front line.

item.title: Germany does not surrender
item.description: The historical end date passes with the Reich still fighting, and better equipped than its enemies.

item.title: The Pan-Atlantic Alliance
item.description: The Western allies formalise a partnership built on shared enemies and unshared secrets.

item.title: The bombs fall — and something else is buried
item.description: The atomic strikes on Japan do not end the war. The Shibito programme begins filling the gaps.

item.title: The Emperor’s laboratories
item.description: Japan stabilises its own Rift programme on Iwo Jima and changes the Pacific war.

item.title: The Science Cities answer
item.description: Soviet genetic programmes field the Ursus: eight feet of man and bear.

item.title: The Schreckwulfen take the field
item.description: Germany’s serum programme produces its first werewolf shock troops, and they work.

item.title: "As one nation under God"
item.description: Roosevelt reframes the war as a crusade against fascism and godless Communism alike.

item.title: The President walks out of the Rift
item.description: A dying Roosevelt enters the Los Alamos Rift and returns restored, certain he has heard God.

item.title: Paris liberated, the countryside isn’t
item.description: De Gaulle enters Paris. Outside the city, the dead are still walking the fields.

item.title: Overlord meets the dead
item.description: The Normandy landings go in against undead shock regiments instead of a broken garrison.

item.title: The Necromobilization programme
item.description: Dresden’s dead are conscripted. The Totenkorps becomes an industrial process.

item.title: The Green Vault steps out
item.description: The cabal abandons secrecy, purges the Nazi leadership and founds the Neu Republik.

item.title: Dresden burns, and opens
item.description: Within a month of Trinity, an atomic bomb destroys Dresden. A second Rift opens at its centre.

item.title: Trinity: the first Rift
item.description: American atomic testing at Los Alamos does not merely succeed. It opens something.

item.title: The Vault in the shadows
item.description: A conspiracy older than the Reich continues to steer Germany from behind its institutions.
